items.hed: The Astros hired Brad Ausmus, a 10-year Houston catcher and former big-league manager, to be their next manager, bringing him back to the organization where he says he always pictured himself
items.insight: Ausmus, 57, spent the last three seasons as the Yankees' bench coach and has five years of managing experience with the Tigers (2014-17, an AL Central title in 2014) and Angels (2019), going a combined 386-422, according to MLB.com. At his introductory news conference at Daikin Park, Ausmus said his focus is the 2027 Astros and the goal every year should be winning the World Series, not just making the playoffs. He is close to senior adviser Jeff Bagwell, a former teammate who was involved in the hiring process; the move comes about two weeks after Houston hired Randy Flores as general manager.

items.hed: Alperen Sengun scored 43 points and grabbed 12 rebounds as the Rockets held off Utah 125-118 Friday night at Toyota Center, handing the Jazz their 11th straight loss and improving Houston to 9-3
items.insight: The win came in NBA Cup group-play, with Sengun posting a career-high scoring night alongside Fred VanVleet and Amen Thompson in the rotation, according to the league's official game page. Utah has now lost 11 in a row and remains well under .500 on the season.
